correctness.rationale: PASS: For each primitive word with k right visits the signed monomial derivative splits into d=gcd(M,k) coordinate cycles of length M/d. Every cycle has at least k/d right-step doubling exponents, implying log2 chi>=k/(Mn) for d>1, while d=1 yields 1/M. Any d>1 forces k>=p, and a primitive p-right word with adjacent right visits realizes the sharp bound. Conversely equality for n>p enforces k=d=p and a zero left gap. Circularly nonadjacent p-subsets are n/p*C(n-p-1,p-1), and proper-power p-right words have all gaps positive: therefore division by n counts primitive cycles. Small n<=p and n=1 handled. Independent finite symbolic verification re-enumerated 56 (M,n) pairs, M=4..10, n=1..8; finite tests do not replace proof.
